appraisal_events.evidence: "il y avait chez Mme de Guermantes une véritable grandeur qui consistait à effacer entièrement tout ce que d'autres n'eussent qu'incomplètement oublié"; "on avait l'impression d'une sorte de purification."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly praises Mme de Guermantes's ability to completely erase past grievances and treat him with unreserved, noble amiability, framing this as genuine greatness of character.

appraisal_events.evidence: "il ne tendit pas la main à Bloch, mais chaque fois que celui-ci lui adressa la parole il lui répondit de l'air le plus insolent, d'une voix irritée et blessante"; Bloch left "éreinté" and did not speak to the narrator for six months.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus publicly refuses to shake Bloch's hand and answers him with contemptuous, wounding insolence at the theatre, humiliating Bloch in front of the narrator after Bloch had been led to expect friendliness.

status_effects.explanation: Her local standing rises through the narrator's admiring account of her capacity to forget past coldness and remain naturally gracious.
Bloch is publicly snubbed and insulted by Charlus in a social setting, after having been led to expect cordiality, which visibly humiliates him.
Bloch is left exhausted and distressed, wrongly believing the narrator had undermined him, and avoids the narrator for six months.

ambiguities: The narrator flags that the true motive behind Charlus's furious reaction to Bloch will only be explained later in the novel ('Sodome I'), so the surface reading of mere caprice or offense may not be the full story, even though the local social effect on Bloch (humiliation) is clear.
